newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia posts poor job figures, dollar drops.
newsitem.headline: Australia posts poor job figures, dollar drops.

text.p: Australia was hit by more soft economic data on Thursday when the bureau of statistics announced a smaller-than-expected rise in June employment.
A rise of 11,900 in the total number of employed helped push the headline unemployment rate down to 8.5 percent from 8.8 percent in June.
But the figure was well below median market forecasts of a 40,000 rise and masked a fall of 16,900 in the number of people in full-time work.
The Australian dollar slipped and bond futures firmed on a feeling that the soft data would put pressure on the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) to cut official interest rates again.
The dollar fell to US$0.7410/15 from US$0.7439/44 shortly after the jobs data was released at 0130 GMT.

The RBA has cut the cash rate four times in the past year, each time by half a percentage point. But the rate cuts have yet to flow through fully to consumer and business confidence and create a feel-good factor for the government.
Economists said the figures, and especially the drop in full-time employment, increased the likelihood of another rate cut in coming weeks to at least 60 percent.
Bill Evans, chief economist at Westpac Banking Corp, said the data was weaker than indicated by the headline unemployment rate. "So it leaves the way open for another rate cut," Evans added.
